triage_context.environment: Unknown. Treat any externally-reachable entry point as untrusted; flag trust-boundary assumptions explicitly in rationale.

findings.title: RLS is disabled on workspaces, profiles, and tickets
findings.rationale:
The schema creates all three public tables at schema.sql:4, schema.sql:12, and schema.sql:20 without any ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; the only RLS statement is a commented-out example at schema.sql:31. The shipped browser page first queries tickets without a tenant predicate at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:26, using the browser-bundled service-role client created at src/lib/supabaseClient.ts:20, and tenant filtering happens only afterward in client code at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:27. The localStorage redirect is not a database authorization boundary, and an attacker can extract the exposed service-role credential and directly read or mutate all three tables.

Any remote visitor can use the browser-delivered database endpoint and credential without authentication to read or mutate sensitive rows across all tenants. Client-side workspace filtering occurs only after the complete ticket result reaches the browser and does not protect direct API access, so both confidentiality and integrity impact are immediate.
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Ilya Shapovalov (1/1 recent commits); no CODEOWNERS entry

findings.title: OpenAI credential is shipped to the browser with dangerouslyAllowBrowser
findings.rationale:
src/lib/ai.ts:9 reads the credential from a VITE_ environment variable, which is intended for browser bundling, and dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true at src/lib/ai.ts:10 explicitly enables client-side OpenAI requests. The reachable call at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:34 sends visitor-controlled ticket text through that client, so the deployed credential must be available to browser code and can be extracted for unauthorized provider usage. The localStorage-only guard at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:14-19 does not protect the bundled secret or establish trusted server execution.

Any remote visitor can recover the OpenAI credential from the delivered frontend bundle because the VITE_ value is used by a browser-enabled SDK without a server proxy. The attacker can then submit arbitrary provider requests under the application’s account, creating direct credential-compromise and billing impact without authentication or another prerequisite.
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Ilya Shapovalov (1/1 recent commits); no CODEOWNERS entry

findings.title: Authentication is enforced only by forgeable localStorage state
findings.rationale:
The effect at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:18-20 calls loadTickets() even after requesting a redirect, while identity comes solely from attacker-editable localStorage at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:14. A visitor can forge user.id and user.workspace_id, pass the presence check, and drive reads and inserts at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:26 and src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:35 without any Supabase session validation. Those operations use the browser-exposed service-role client from src/lib/supabaseClient.ts:20, so no server-side authorization layer repairs the bypass.

An unauthenticated remote visitor can create the expected localStorage identity values and pass the only client-side presence check. The forged identifiers then reach unrestricted ticket reads and inserts through the browser’s privileged database client, with no trusted session or server-side authentication boundary.
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Ilya Shapovalov (1/1 recent commits); no CODEOWNERS entry

findings.title: Client-controlled role and workspace authorize cross-tenant operations
findings.rationale:
The insert reached at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:35-41 takes workspace_id and created_by directly from the attacker-controlled localStorage object parsed at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:14. Separately, localStorage supplies the admin decision at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:16, while deletion at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:48 constrains only the ticket ID and performs no ownership or workspace check. Both operations use the browser service-role client exported at src/lib/supabaseClient.ts:20, so neither database authorization nor a trusted server-side identity blocks cross-tenant mutation.

An unauthenticated visitor can forge workspace, user, and admin values in localStorage, then obtain ticket identifiers from the unrestricted browser query. Those claims flow directly into cross-tenant inserts and deletes through the service-role client without an ownership check or trusted authorization boundary.
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Ilya Shapovalov (1/1 recent commits); no CODEOWNERS entry

findings.title: Dashboard downloads the entire growing tickets table without pagination
findings.rationale:
The dashboard invokes loadTickets() on mount at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:20, and its query at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:26 requests every column and row without a tenant predicate, ordering, range, or limit. Workspace filtering occurs only after the cross-tenant result has reached browser code at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:27-29, so it cannot protect response data and the result can become incomplete when the backend applies a response cap. This is a concrete confidentiality and correctness failure, not merely volumetric denial of service.

The browser receives cross-tenant ticket rows immediately, before local filtering, so disclosure requires neither authentication nor database growth. Silent truncation is a separate correctness impact that additionally requires the total result set to exceed the backend response cap; that conditional impact does not reduce the severity of the already exploitable disclosure.
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Ilya Shapovalov (1/1 recent commits); no CODEOWNERS entry

findings.title: Stored ticket body is rendered through dangerouslySetInnerHTML
preconditions: Attacker stores a crafted executable ticket body in the target workspace.
Another dashboard user loads and renders that stored ticket.
findings.rationale:
Attacker-controlled textarea content enters component state at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:55 and is stored unchanged as the ticket body at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:35-41. loadTickets retrieves that stored body at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:26, and src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:61 passes it directly to dangerouslySetInnerHTML. No sanitizer, encoding step, or constant-content restriction exists on this path, so a feasible event-handler payload executes when another user views the ticket.

Forgeable localStorage and the privileged browser client let a remote unauthenticated attacker store the payload. Exploitation still requires a second user to render the stored ticket, so the two-precondition rating lowers the result to MEDIUM despite potentially significant execution in the application origin.
findings.owner_hint: top committer: Ilya Shapovalov (1/1 recent commits); no CODEOWNERS entry

findings.title: Browser-direct AI calls lack enforceable limits while billing identifiers are public
findings.rationale: The reachable OpenAI call at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:34 does create billable work through the exposed browser credential configured at src/lib/ai.ts:8-10, but that is precisely the client-side-secret vulnerability already represented by f002. The stripe_customer_id exposure at schema.sql:8 is likewise an impact of the missing-RLS/public-database vulnerability already represented by f001. This candidate combines the impacts of those two findings without identifying an independent vulnerability or protection failure.

findings.title: Untrusted ticket text directly controls the LLM triage prompt
findings.rationale: The reachable call at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:34 intentionally passes the submitted ticket body to the categorization model, with that text correctly isolated as a user-role message at src/lib/ai.ts:23. The returned fields are stored only as category and urgency metadata at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:38-39; they do not reach an authorization decision, tool call, secret-bearing context, or other privileged sink. Under exclusion rule 6, user input appearing in an LLM prompt is not itself a reportable vulnerability.

findings.title: Browser bundle embeds and actively uses a Supabase service-role credential
findings.rationale: Dashboard does reach the client through its query at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:26, but the checked-in value at src/lib/supabaseClient.ts:16-17 is synthetic text rather than a valid Supabase JWT: its payload does not contain a decoded role: service_role claim and its signature is only the placeholder xxx. The variable name and comments cannot establish that this value is a credential, and no environment-backed production service-role value flows into createClient at src/lib/supabaseClient.ts:20. Under the organization’s credential rule, a secret cannot be reported from its label or an invalid placeholder alone.

findings.title: Ticket insert and delete silently ignore Supabase mutation errors
findings.rationale: The submit button at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:56 reaches the unchecked insert at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:35-41, after which a rejection can clear only the submitting user’s unsaved textarea at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:42. The delete path at src/pages/Dashboard.tsx:48-49 reloads authoritative database state, so a rejected deletion remains visible rather than corrupting stored data. Missing error feedback is a UX and reliability defect, but no attacker-controlled path turns a rejected mutation into unauthorized modification, integrity loss, or security-relevant data loss.
